task_summary: Generate comprehensive onboarding documentation for the egg repository that helps new contributors understand the project, its architecture, and how to contribute effectively.

codebase_analysis.project_description: egg is a structurally enforced SDLC pipeline for autonomous LLM agents that turns GitHub issues into reviewed pull requests with mandatory human gates. It consists of three Docker containers (gateway, orchestrator, sandbox) plus shared libraries, CLI tools, and GitHub Actions workflows.

codebase_size.gateway: ~30 Python files, ~8000+ lines (policy enforcement, credential injection, API proxy)
codebase_size.orchestrator: 33 Python files + 8 route modules, ~10,400 lines (pipeline management, container lifecycle, HITL)
codebase_size.sandbox: ~20 Python files in egg_lib + scripts/git (870 lines) + scripts/gh (1,227 lines) + entrypoint.py (1,584 lines)
codebase_size.shared: 51 Python files across 6 packages (egg_config, egg_container, egg_contracts, egg_logging, egg_git, egg_orchestrator)
codebase_size.tests_unit: 29+ test files across tests/, gateway/tests/ (18,037 lines), orchestrator/tests/ (9,454 lines), tests/sandbox/ (10,761 lines)
codebase_size.tests_integration: 16+ test files in integration_tests/ + local_pipeline/ + sdlc/ + deployment_validation/
codebase_size.action: 14 files (GitHub Action composite action, prompt builders, conventions)
codebase_size.docs: 15+ READMEs, 10 ADRs, 7+ guides, templates, and strategy docs

key_components.name: Gateway Sidecar
key_components.role: Trusted enforcement engine - policy enforcement, credential injection, network filtering, SDLC phase validation
key_files: gateway.py - Main HTTP server with git/gh API endpoints
policy.py - Branch ownership, push policies, reviewer identity
phase_filter.py - Phase-based operation filtering and file restrictions
agent_restrictions.py - Agent role-based file access enforcement
contract_api.py - Contract API endpoints for role-based mutations
token_refresher.py - GitHub App token management
anthropic_credentials.py - API key injection for Claude
checkpoint_handler.py - Checkpoint capture (commit + session-end)
worktree_manager.py - Git worktree lifecycle
session_manager.py - Agent session management

key_components.name: Orchestrator
key_components.role: Local SDLC pipeline execution, state management, container lifecycle, multi-agent wave coordination, HITL decisions
key_files: api.py - REST API server (8 blueprints)
models.py - Pydantic models for pipeline state (Pipeline, PhaseExecution, AgentExecution, HITLDecision)
state_store.py - Git-backed pipeline state persistence (792 lines, atomic ops, per-pipeline locks)
multi_agent.py - Wave-based parallel agent execution (AgentWave, MultiAgentExecutor)
container_spawner.py - Gateway-integrated container lifecycle
decision_queue.py - HITL queue, polling, resolution with debounce
dispatch.py - Agent dispatch logic bridging egg_contracts with orchestrator
events.py - Pub/sub event bus with 16+ event types
dag_visualizer.py - Pipeline execution graph visualization
routes/ - API route handlers (pipelines, phases, signals, decisions, containers, checks, health, metrics)
key_components.note: The orchestrator has NO dedicated README.md - this is an identified documentation gap.

key_components.name: Sandbox Container
key_components.role: Untrusted agent execution environment with no credentials and restricted network
key_files: entrypoint.py - Container startup: user setup, git config, gateway health, Claude Code launch
egg_lib/cli.py - Host CLI entry point (egg command, 346 lines)
egg_lib/sdlc_cli.py - SDLC pipeline CLI (596 lines)
egg_lib/contract_cli.py - SDLC contract CLI (1,217 lines)
egg_lib/orch_cli.py - Orchestrator API CLI (1,256 lines)
scripts/git - Git wrapper routing all ops through gateway (870 lines)
scripts/gh - GitHub CLI wrapper with policy enforcement (1,227 lines)
llm/claude/runner.py - Claude Code runner (415 lines)
.claude/rules/ - Agent behavior rules (8 files combined into ~/CLAUDE.md)
.claude/commands/ - Custom slash commands (/sdlc, /coder-mode, etc.)

key_components.name: Shared Libraries
key_components.role: Cross-container utilities used by gateway, orchestrator, and sandbox
packages: egg_config/ - Configuration utilities, centralized constants (ports, networks, container names, devserver limits), validators
egg_container/ - Shared container-launch config builder (build_sandbox_config, build_sandbox_docker_cmd, git_shadow_mounts)

egg_contracts/ - SDLC contract models (Pydantic), plan parser (3 modes: YAML fence, YAML front matter, markdown regex), role-based validation, phase checks, agent roles, dependency graph, agent recovery, checkpoints, redactor
egg_orchestrator/ - Sandbox-to-orchestrator communication (OrchestratorClient, signal types, detection utilities)
prompts/ - Shared review criteria (code-review, agent-design, contract-review, autofixer-rules)

key_components.name: GitHub Action
key_components.role: Composite action for running egg in GitHub Actions CI/CD
key_files: action.yml - Action metadata (inputs, outputs)
entrypoint.sh - Main orchestration (gateway + sandbox setup)
generate-config.sh - Runtime config from action inputs
build-review-prompt.sh, build-autofixer-prompt.sh, etc. - Context-specific prompt builders
review-conventions.md, autofixer-conventions.md, conflict-conventions.md - Behavior guidelines

key_components.name: SDLC State
key_components.role: Pipeline configuration, schemas, and runtime state
key_files: .egg/phase-permissions.json - Phase-based operation permissions and file restrictions
.egg/contract-rules.md - Contract verification guidelines
.egg/schemas/ - JSON schemas (contract, checkpoint, phase-permissions, yaml-tasks, usage)
.egg-state/contracts/ - Per-pipeline contract JSON files
.egg-state/drafts/ - Analysis and plan documents
.egg-state/reviews/ - Code/design review outputs
.egg-state/agent-outputs/ - Agent execution outputs
.egg-state/checks/ - Check execution results

architecture_patterns.security_model: Infrastructure enforcement (not behavioral). Gateway physically blocks operations. Sandbox has no credentials, no .git/ access, no merge capability. Zero-trust boundary between containers.
architecture_patterns.sdlc_pipeline: Refine -> Plan -> Implement -> PR, with mandatory human gates at refine and plan boundaries. Phase permissions enforced by gateway via phase-permissions.json.
architecture_patterns.multi_agent: Wave-based parallel execution. Coder first, then Tester+Documenter in parallel, then Integrator. Reviewers run after workers complete. Max parallelism configurable.
architecture_patterns.state_management: Git-backed pipeline state in orchestrator (orphan branch). SDLC contracts as JSON committed to feature branches for auditability.
architecture_patterns.credential_isolation: Anthropic API via gateway proxy, GitHub tokens via gateway wrappers, sandbox never sees raw credentials.
architecture_patterns.network_modes: Public mode (full internet + credential injection) vs Private mode (Anthropic API only + private repos only). Squid proxy with domain allowlisting.

entry_points: README.md (437 lines) - Comprehensive project overview, architecture diagrams, CLI reference, quick start
docs/index.md (118 lines) - Master navigation hub (agent-oriented), task-specific guide lookup table
CONTRIBUTING.md (118 lines) - Development setup, workflow, PR process
architecture_docs: docs/architecture/README.md - System design, security model, SDLC contracts, checkpoint system
guides: docs/guides/local-quickstart.md - Getting started with PAT auth
development_docs: docs/development/TEST_COVERAGE_PLAN.md (439 lines) - Test coverage improvement strategy

identified_gaps.title: No progressive onboarding path
identified_gaps.description: Documentation jumps between high-level architecture and implementation details. README.md immediately presents gateway diagrams, phase permissions tables, and full CLI reference. No narrative path from 'what is this?' to 'how do I contribute?'
identified_gaps.impact: New contributors must piece together a mental model from scattered docs

identified_gaps.title: Agent-oriented vs human-oriented navigation
identified_gaps.description: docs/index.md is explicitly designed for agents navigating the codebase. No equivalent human-oriented onboarding guide exists.
identified_gaps.impact: Human contributors lack a clear starting point

identified_gaps.title: Missing orchestrator/README.md
identified_gaps.description: The orchestrator is a major component (33 production Python files, ~10,400 lines, manages the entire SDLC pipeline lifecycle) but has no dedicated README. Every other major component directory (gateway/, sandbox/, shared/, config/, bin/, action/) has one.
identified_gaps.impact: Contributors working on orchestrator changes have no component-level documentation

identified_gaps.title: Test infrastructure not explained for contributors
identified_gaps.description: The test suite has 4 test directories (tests/, gateway/tests/, orchestrator/tests/, integration_tests/), 5 markers (integration, functional, e2e, security, agent_flaky), Docker-based integration fixtures, but no guide explaining patterns for writing tests. TEST_COVERAGE_PLAN.md focuses on coverage improvement strategy, not how to write tests.
identified_gaps.impact: New contributors may write tests incorrectly or not know which test directory to use

identified_gaps.title: No conceptual overview synthesizing key concepts
identified_gaps.description: Rich conceptual model (trusted vs untrusted containers, structural enforcement vs behavioral controls, phase-based permissions, multi-agent orchestration, credential isolation) is documented across ADRs and architecture docs but not synthesized into a newcomer-friendly overview.
identified_gaps.impact: Conceptual understanding requires reading multiple documents

identified_gaps.title: No contributor workflow examples
identified_gaps.description: CONTRIBUTING.md covers setup and make targets but doesn't walk through common contribution scenarios (fixing a gateway bug, adding a CLI command, modifying phase permissions, adding a new agent role).
identified_gaps.impact: Contributors may not know the best approach for specific task types

recommended_approach.strategy: Option B from refine analysis: Onboarding Guide + Gap-Filling Component Docs
recommended_approach.rationale: Addresses both the immediate need (clear onboarding path) and the underlying gaps (missing orchestrator README, undocumented test patterns). Follows established conventions — every major component already has a README, guides live in docs/guides/. The refine reviewers approved this approach.

deliverables.description: Primary onboarding document: progressive learning path from zero to contributor
structure: 1. What is egg? (1 paragraph concept: sandboxed SDLC pipeline for LLM agents)
2. Key Concepts (trusted vs untrusted, structural enforcement, SDLC phases, agent roles, credential isolation, network modes)
3. Architecture at a Glance (simplified diagram + component table, link to full architecture docs)
4. How the SDLC Pipeline Works (refine -> plan -> implement -> merge, with human gates)
5. Getting Started (prerequisites, development setup via CONTRIBUTING.md, local quickstart link)
6. Repository Layout (condensed from STRUCTURE.md with annotations for newcomers)
7. Common Contribution Scenarios (table: task type -> which docs to read -> which directories to modify)
8. Testing Your Changes (which test directory, how to run, markers explained, link to testing guide)
9. Where to Go Next (links to component READMEs, guides, ADRs by interest area)
constraints: Link to existing docs, never duplicate content
Focus on stable concepts (architecture, security model, workflows), not volatile implementation details
Keep under 300 lines to avoid 'mega document' problem
Write for human contributors (the primary audience), not agents

deliverables.description: Component README following the established pattern of gateway/README.md and sandbox/README.md
structure: 1. Overview (what the orchestrator does, how it fits in the architecture)
2. API Reference (key endpoints with brief descriptions)
3. Pipeline Lifecycle (phase management, state persistence)
4. Multi-Agent Execution (wave-based model, agent roles, dependency resolution)
5. Container Management (spawning, monitoring, cleanup)
6. HITL Decisions (queue, polling, resolution, timeout)
7. State Management (git-backed state, atomic operations, pipeline isolation)
8. Event System (event bus, SSE streaming, status reporting)
9. Configuration (environment variables, defaults)
10. Development (running locally, testing, key files)
constraints: Follow the pattern of gateway/README.md (~200 lines, component-level detail)
Include a directory structure overview like other READMEs

deliverables.description: Test architecture guide covering how to write and run tests for each component
structure: 1. Test Organization (4 directories, what goes where)
2. Running Tests (make targets, direct pytest, CI parity via act)
3. Test Markers (integration, functional, e2e, security, agent_flaky - when to use each)
4. Key Fixtures (EggStack, gateway_session, test_container for integration tests)
5. Writing Tests by Component (gateway: mock patterns, orchestrator: state store fixtures, sandbox: CLI testing, shared: contract model tests)
6. Integration Test Patterns (Docker setup, health checks, compose-based tests)
7. Coverage Goals (80% overall, 95% for security-critical, reference TEST_COVERAGE_PLAN.md for improvement strategy)
constraints: Complement (not duplicate) TEST_COVERAGE_PLAN.md — testing.md explains HOW to write tests, TEST_COVERAGE_PLAN.md tracks coverage improvement STRATEGY
Include practical examples showing the pattern for each component
Keep under 200 lines — this is a contributor guide, not an exhaustive reference

implementation_order: 1. Research and draft orchestrator/README.md (DOC-2) — fills the biggest component gap and provides material for the onboarding guide to reference
2. Research and draft docs/guides/testing.md (DOC-3) — fills the testing documentation gap
3. Draft docs/guides/onboarding.md (DOC-1) — the main deliverable, can now reference all component docs
4. Update docs/index.md (DOC-4) — add links to new docs
5. Update README.md (DOC-5) — add new contributors callout
dependencies: DOC-1 references DOC-2 (orchestrator README) and DOC-3 (testing guide), so those should be written first
DOC-4 and DOC-5 are minimal updates that depend on DOC-1 being complete

technical_decisions.decision: Use Option B (Onboarding Guide + Gap-Filling) over Option A (standalone guide only) or Option C (restructure index.md)
technical_decisions.rationale: Fills structural documentation gaps while creating the onboarding path. Option A leaves the orchestrator README and test guide gaps. Option C compromises the agent-oriented design of docs/index.md.
alternatives_considered: Restructure docs/index.md to serve both humans and agents

technical_decisions.rationale: The refine reviewer flagged that TEST_COVERAGE_PLAN.md (439 lines) already exists. testing.md focuses on HOW to write tests (patterns, fixtures, which directory to use), while TEST_COVERAGE_PLAN.md tracks the STRATEGY for improving coverage. Different audiences, different purposes.

technical_decisions.decision: Create orchestrator/README.md following gateway/README.md pattern (~200 lines)
technical_decisions.rationale: The orchestrator is the only major component without a README. Following the established pattern of gateway/README.md ensures consistency and gives contributors a familiar format.
The guide is meant to be a progressive learning path that links to existing docs. If it becomes a 'mega document', it becomes hard to maintain and defeats the purpose of progressive disclosure.

technical_decisions.decision: Write for human contributors as the primary audience
technical_decisions.rationale: Agents already have docs/index.md as their navigation hub. The gap is human contributor onboarding.

constraints: No content duplication — link to existing docs, especially the 15+ READMEs and 7+ guides
Cross-cutting docs go in docs/, component docs stay close to code
Documentation should be maintainable by the on-push-doc-updater workflow
Focus on stable concepts (architecture, security model, contribution workflow), not volatile implementation details
The repository is under heavy development — onboarding docs should be resilient to code changes

risks.risk: Content drift — onboarding guide references may become stale as code evolves
risks.mitigation: Focus on linking to existing docs rather than inlining details. The doc-updater workflow flags changes that need doc updates.

risks.risk: Scope creep — temptation to document everything in the onboarding guide
risks.mitigation: Strict 300-line limit for onboarding guide. Focus on progressive disclosure and links.

risks.risk: Orchestrator README accuracy — the orchestrator is complex (33 files, 10,400 lines)
risks.mitigation: Follow gateway/README.md pattern. Focus on API, lifecycle, and configuration. Link to docs/architecture/orchestrator.md for deployment details.
